ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic illumination triangle, with A at the lower left, B at the upper left, and C on the right; AB is marked as a certain latitude line, BC is a meridian, and AC is the terminator line. Beside point C it is marked “(0°,30°W),” indicating that C is on the equator and on the 30°W meridian; on the left there is an arrow labeled “rotation direction”; the stem gives ∠BAC=70°, and point A's local time is 12 o'clock, with the sun just on the horizon. Then reason: According to the relationship between the figure and the text, A is a point in the Northern Hemisphere that is still on the terminator line at noon, that is, the critical latitude line of polar day or polar night; ∠BAC=70° determines that the latitude line where A is located is 70°N. The noon solar altitude at point A is h=0°. Using the noon solar altitude formula h=90°-|φ-δ|, substitute φ=70°N, obtaining 0°=90°-|70°-δ|, so δ=-20°, and the subsolar latitude is 20°S. Judging from the rotation direction in the figure, AC is the dusk line at C, and the local time on the dusk line at the equator is 18 o'clock; the longitude of point C is 30°W. The local time on the subsolar meridian is 12 o'clock, which differs from C's 18 o'clock by 6 hours, namely a longitude difference of 90°; the meridian where it is 12 o'clock is 90° west of point C, therefore the subsolar meridian is 30°W westward by 90° = 120°W. Combining these, the coordinates of the subsolar point are 20°S,120°W.

<image1>

At this time, what are the coordinates of the subsolar point?

Then reason: According to the relationship between the figure and the text, A is a point in the Northern Hemisphere that is still on the terminator line at noon, that is, the critical latitude line of polar day or polar night; ∠BAC=70° determines that the latitude line where A is located is 70°N. The noon solar altitude at point A is h=0°. Using the noon solar altitude formula h=90°-|φ-δ|, substitute φ=70°N, obtaining 0°=90°-|70°-δ|, so δ=-20°, and the subsolar latitude is 20°S. Judging from the rotation direction in the figure, AC is the dusk line at C, and the local time on the dusk line at the equator is 18 o'clock; the longitude of point C is 30°W. The local time on the subsolar meridian is 12 o'clock, which differs from C's 18 o'clock by 6 hours, namely a longitude difference of 90°; the meridian where it is 12 o'clock is 90° west of point C, therefore the subsolar meridian is 30°W westward by 90° = 120°W. Combining these, the coordinates of the subsolar point are 20°S,120°W.

critic_agent_reviews.critic_suggestions: 推理整体与题意、图像和标准答案一致，且遵循了“先描述图像，再推理”的顺序。可小幅改进之处是补充说明为什么图中∠BAC=70°可对应判定A所在纬线为70°N，以及“由自转方向判断AC在C处为昏线”的判读依据，但不影响结论。

该推理总体通过。图像描述先于推理，符合“先描述图像，再推理”的顺序要求；关键视觉信息如A/B/C位置、C标注为(0°,30°W)、AC为晨昏线、左侧自转方向箭头等与图像和题干一致。推理路线基本忠实于方法草稿：由A点正午太阳在地平线判断北半球极夜边界，由∠BAC=70°推出临界纬线70°N，再得太阳直射纬度20°S；再依据C为赤道昏线交点，地方时18时，推出直射经线为30°W以西90°即120°W。最终答案与标准答案一致。小建议：'由图中∠BAC=70°，按题设几何关系可判定该临界纬线为70°N'这一句可略加说明其几何依据，避免显得跳步；另外图中角度数值主要来自题干，图像只显示角标，表述为“题干给出∠BAC=70°”会更严谨。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The following figure is an illumination diagram at a certain moment in the Northern Hemisphere. AB is a certain latitude line, AC is the terminator line, BC is a meridian, ∠BAC=70°, at this time the local time at point A is 12 o'clock, and the sun is just on the horizon.

<image1>

At this time, what are the coordinates of the subsolar point?
